alt: A double-height hall with freestanding stone chimney and wrapping staircase, lit late evening by a single aged-bronze pendant light, walls in deep sea-green zellige tiles, warm terracotta floor, and soft lime plaster ceiling.
text:
colour stopped hedging here.

sea-green zellige catches the evening light. terracotta grounds it. soft plaster breathes above. each material stands its own — no hedge, no whisper. five schemes cycling through jewel tones and warm earth. late evening, one pool of light. this is deep saturation as material decision, not decoration.

#colourmaximalism #interiorcolour #unhedged #colourforward #brutalist

provenance.base_prompt: A double-height hall, camera positioned well back on the ground level to the left of center, so a monumental freestanding chimney breast — raw stone and unfired clay brick — rises off-axis, the entire room's geometry turning around it. The staircase, cantilevered timber treads with stone stringers, wraps the chimney's far side. A single statement pendant of aged bronze and mouth-blown glass hangs in the upper void, casting one pool of warm lamplight across the staircase landing and chimney face, the rest of the space in deep shadow: late evening. The far wall is fully glazed, opening onto a steep pine hillside dropping away below. Ground level: a monumental stone plinth table, twelve feet long, angled to the room, its surface scattered with stacked books, pale ceramic vessels, and dark sculptural stones; beside it, a deep unfinished timber shelving wall, floor to ceiling, laden with books spine-out, ceramics in neutral tones, smooth dark stones, a single brass vessel, dried grasses in ceramic, layered textiles woven into the display; an unfinished timber bench runs along the chimney's lower run; a sculptural timber chair with woven paper-light seat sits in the far reach where lamplight barely reaches it; a large woven hanging in neutral fiber hangs beside the shelving, adding texture to the vertical plane. The upper level, visible beyond the staircase turn, shows the shadowed outline of a reading nook carved into the architecture. Aged raw concrete floor throughout, marked and patinated by time, warm where the lamp reaches it, cool in shadow. All walkways remain clear and functional. The composition reads as deliberate, brutalist, inhabited — the entire room organized around the chimney's sculptural presence
